content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent patterns when extending AI function calling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through adding tool handlers with safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides review of backend/main.py before adding a new tool.
Shows how to create a backend helper function with error handling.
Explains how to register an OpenAI function definition.
Shows where to wire the tool into the WebSocket message loop.
Prompts review of agent mode and chat mode restrictions.
Reminds authors to add timeouts, avoid secrets, and document purpose.
limitations: It provides implementation guidance, not a complete generated backend feature.
It assumes a backend/main.py structure with an OpenAI function calling system.
It does not automatically validate the security of the finished tool.
Risky tools still require human review before deployment.

use_cases.title: Add a Read-Only Backend Tool
use_cases.description: Create a safe utility tool that reads data and returns a structured result to the agent.

use_cases.title: Extend an AI Agent Capability
use_cases.description: Register a new function definition and connect it to the backend message loop.

use_cases.title: Review Tool Access Boundaries
use_cases.description: Check whether a new tool belongs in agent mode only or can be exposed to chat mode.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a read-only backend tool that returns repository status. Follow existing patterns and include error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Wire a Tool Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a helper function, register its function schema, and add the WebSocket handler for a directory listing tool.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Restricted Network Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add a safe web lookup tool with timeout handling. Keep it unavailable in chat mode unless it is read-only.

prompt_templates.title: Review a New Agent Capability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a git operations tool, document its purpose, define mode restrictions, and flag unsafe actions before implementation.

output_examples.input: Add a tool to list directory contents.
output_examples.output: A backend implementation plan with helper creation, function registration, handler wiring, and chat-mode safety review.

output_examples.input: Create a tool for git operations.
output: Defines the tool purpose and expected parameters.
Adds timeout and error handling guidance.
Limits destructive operations unless explicitly reviewed.

output_examples.output: A safer tool plan that includes timeout requirements, scope limits, and agent-only access unless the behavior is read-only.

best_practices: Review existing backend patterns before adding a new tool.
Keep chat-mode tools read-only unless a safety review approves more access.
Add timeouts, error handling, and clear function documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not expose destructive actions to chat mode without review.
Do not hardcode API keys, tokens, or other secrets.
Do not add long-running operations without timeout protection.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps add backend tools for an OpenAI function calling system.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete tool automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation steps that the agent applies to the existing backend.

faq.question: Which files does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a backend/main.py file with tool definitions and a WebSocket message loop.

faq.question: Can it support Claude and Codex workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it address safety?
faq.answer: It asks authors to review mode restrictions, use timeouts, handle errors, and avoid hardcoded secrets.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Backend developers, AI product engineers, and reviewers who maintain agent tool systems can use it.
